cap.name: 64k
cap.source: M4.1 (T8 memory gate on the B200): 64K passes

bands.definition: mean pass rate of the six labelled models: easy >= 2/3, medium >= 1/3, hard > 0, unsolved 0

budget_rule.throughput_source: measured on real 64K rows through apex_train.sft on GPU-T: steady-state median 8,898 tok/s of the sft_pilot run logs/sft_pilot_lr1e4_20261012_083749 (M4.1's synthetic T7: 8.8K)
budget_rule.rule:
the main SFT run must finish inside `max_hours` (plan: ~7.5 to 8 h) at the throughput measured at the
chosen cap (M4.1, T7). Every sequence token of the mixture (training rows and validation shard, as the plan's sizing
table counts them) is costed at that throughput. When the mixture does not fit, whole units are trimmed in this order:
1. Python SWE rows: SWE-rebench-V2 Python first, then Scale-SWE, each the last drawn first (the draw puts large tasks
   first, so the random-phase rows go first); Go / JS / TS rows are never trimmed;
2. retention rows, proportionally across its parts, down to a 12 percent loss-token floor;
3. whole terminal episodes, TerminalHorizon before TermGrade, proportionally across the category-quota groups.

eval_overhead.note: estimate [I]: forward-only passes assumed ~3x faster per token than a training step with gradient checkpointing

normalisation: The trainer's loss is token-weighted: the sum of token losses divided by the trained (assistant-mask) tokens of the accumulation window, so a slice's gradient share equals its loss-token share; sequence-token shares set the training time. Both are recorded.

freeze.requires: p1_pools current, p2_rows over exactly these train/dev files with zero drops, Dean's review
